sentences.1: Natural selection acts wherever there are things that vary, that pass on what they are, and that leave different numbers of descendants because of it.
sentences.3: A group whose members help one another at a cost to themselves leaves more descendant groups than a group of members who do not, because the helping group outlasts, outgrows or outfights its rivals.
sentences.4: Within any one group, a member who helps does worse than a member who does not, because the helper pays the cost and every member shares the benefit.
sentences.5: So selection within groups works against helping, and selection between groups works for it.
sentences.6: Which wins depends on how much the groups differ from one another and how much the members differ within them.
sentences.7: When groups differ greatly, because helpers cluster together and stay together, selection between groups is the stronger, and helping spreads.
sentences.8: This is a way of speaking, not a cause: the group structure shows the spread of helping, and remove the structure and the spread goes on as before.
sentences.9: Accounting that credits the spread to the individual's relatives is arithmetic done afterwards, and it does not change what produced the outcome.
sentences.10: Where cooperation has spread, as in the social insects, the cell, and the human tribe, groups were the things selection was acting on.

leftover: Sentence 1: “Natural selection acts wherever there are things that vary, that pass on what they are, and that leave different numbers of descendants because of it.” — The criterion joins variation, inheritance and causally different descendant numbers. The numeric reproductive condition and joint explanation are outside scope; dropping it would weaken the selection criterion.
Sentence 2: “Groups can be such things.” — Can is a possibility claim. It is not an assertion that an actual group satisfies all selection conditions.

Sentence 3: “A group whose members help one another at a cost to themselves leaves more descendant groups than a group of members who do not, because the helping group outlasts, outgrows or outfights its rivals.” — Conditional comparison of descendant counts, costly helping, and alternative rival outcomes. No single outlasts/outgrows/outfights disjunct is asserted; no numeric reproduction law is substituted.

Sentence 4: “because the helper pays the cost and every member shares the benefit” — The conjunction supplies several explanatory contributors; no single one is substituted for the combined reason. Amounts of cost/benefit and reproductive performance are not computed.
Sentence 5: “So” — Inference is from the quantified comparisons in sentences 3–4; their full numerical content has no executable reason line. No guessed selection law bridges the bin.

Sentence 6: “Which wins depends on how much the groups differ from one another and how much the members differ within them.” — The dependency is on amounts of variation within and between groups; converting it to mere presence/absence of differences would change the criterion.

Sentence 7: “When groups differ greatly, because helpers cluster together and stay together, selection between groups is the stronger, and helping spreads.” — Greatly and stronger control the conditional conclusion; helpers clustering/staying is inside that explanation, not an independently asserted actual cluster. No quantitative condition is silently dropped.

Sentence 8: “a way of speaking; as before” — Metalinguistic emphasis and sameness of rate/manner through time are not checked. j asks only whether spread persists, not whether its amount or trajectory remains identical.
Sentence 9: “credits the spread to the individual's relatives; afterwards” — Attribution and exact timing of the accounting are not computed. k is a free description, not execution of arithmetic.

readings: Sentence 4. Open readings: worse names an exact reproductive amount or qualitative comparative performance. Chosen: retain only opaque does_worse, not a numeric difference; scope of all rules is generic, no actual helper invented.

Sentence 8. Open readings: remove as withdrawing a statement or making the structure absent. Chosen: MAKE NOT SO; filled in, with f as the reference fact. The ongoing spread is presupposed g, not the future result asserted as an actual premise.

Sentence 9. Open readings: accounting is literally causally efficacious or merely redescribes the cause. Chosen: the sentence explicitly denies changing the producer; no positive accounting-causes-outcome claim.
Sentence 10. Open readings: a causal law or an observational generalisation. Chosen: ALWAYS SHOWS; applies to the three given examples without claiming a mechanism.
